title: Prime Spell Security Guidelines bind Prime Agents even when they exist only in Signal channels or live calls
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.2 defines Prime Spell Security Guidelines as "all security guidelines, requirements, and best practices codified in the Atlas **or communicated to Prime Agents through the official channels used for Prime operations,"** and then enumerates those channels: "(1) designated Signal and Slack channels, (2) documentation authored or provided by Core Spell Teams or other stakeholders, and (3) live calls."

A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.3.1 gives the definition teeth: "Prime Agents must adhere to all Prime Spell Security Guidelines as a condition of inclusion in an Executive Vote," and A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.3.2 designates any breach a Prime Spell Security Incident carrying financial penalties.

This sits in visible tension with the Atlas's own foundation, which locates authority in versioned, citable documents and treats provenance links as the basis for every action. Here the operative rule set includes things said on a call. A Prime can be penalized for violating a requirement that has no section id, no edit history, and no proposal that ratified it.

The justification is temporal and stated in A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.1: the regime exists "during the period when the Prime Spell Security Framework is progressively codified and operationalized in the Atlas." It is an explicit interim trade — enforceability now, at the cost of citability — and the load-bearing question is whether codification actually catches up, because the incentive to formalize a rule weakens once it is already enforceable without formalization.
description: A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.2 sources binding requirements from uncodified channels while compliance gates Executive Vote inclusion — creating obligations that cannot be cited to a fixed text.
